READABILITY.evidence: Names and doc comments are good, and the format layout comment in shapeindex_encode.go helps. But the decode logic leans on single-letter names like `c := decodeClippedShape(...)`, `n := readCount(...)` and `switch x := shape.(type)`, so the cap applies.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: shapeindex_encode.go is 601 lines (over the 500 cap). It ignores the convention of putting per-shape encode/decode next to each type. It hand-writes Polygon, Polyline and Loop payloads instead of reusing their existing decode methods. decodeIndexShape and decodeShapeIndex are each about 75–80 lines.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Every count passes through readCount with a limit, and allocations are capped by maxDecodePrealloc. Cell order, overlap and edge-ID range are checked, and bools are read strictly. `s` is left unchanged on error. The one catch-all `recover()` turns a panic into an error rather than hiding it.

C7-14-CASE1.evidence: Encode and Decode are purely additive. Existing typeTag values and per-shape wire formats are untouched, and the Shape interface is unchanged. The new tags (6, 7, 8) are private to the index format. The only change to existing code is the pendingAdditionsPos/nextID loop fix, which doesn't affect any format.
